description:
Hi, I’m Chris, and I lead Corporate Communications at Ashby. My career has been far from linear: I started in sports journalism, moved into Comms consulting, went in-house at a major bank to do Corporate Strategy, transitioned to a startup to build out their Content function, and earlier this year I joined Ashby’s Content team. The throughline between these roles is storytelling; whether it’s triple-A players to watch out for, how to tell a comprehensive story to investors, or best ways to showcase customer love, it all boils down to finding the most compelling narrative.

What drew me to Ashby, in part, is the clarity of the product and audience. I was an Ashby customer for years as a hiring manager at Modern Treasury, so I saw firsthand how intentional this team is about building a product that makes hiring more effective, intuitive, and human.

While I’ve led a content and comms team before, the function will look a little different at Ashby. As I build out our mandate with our Head of Content, Anum, I’m trying to be thoughtful about scope, strategy, audience, and delivery. We’re a growing team with high standards, and those standards should carry into how we communicate about Ashby as a whole.

That brings me to this role, which I’ve owned since joining and am now evolving and “giving away the legos.” We have a working case study program and a customer base that loves talking about us, and a healthy bench of talent leaders and RecOps practitioners willing to share organic, unprompted love for Ashby. We have come a long way on customer stories, but we’re still only a fraction of the way to what they could become.

This role is about closing that gap by taking ownership of how our customers show up in the world. You’ll work across Marketing, Sales, and CS to scale our case study program, own enablement, and continuously improve the process of our customer content flywheel. In the near term, that means publishing a steady stream of written case studies; in the long term, you’ll define what a best-in-class in-depth customer story looks like at Ashby, from evaluation through implementation and beyond. Volume is important here, and so is depth, and the role is delivering on both.

This role reports to me. I’m looking for someone with editorial taste, and the kind of curiosity that digs deep on how our product solves real TA problems, and a personable demeanor that makes a busy talent leader happy to spend an hour on the phone with you. If that sounds like you, please apply!

What you’ll be responsible for in this role

Own Ashby’s customer storytelling strategy.

Building on a working case study program, you'll rethink our written stories and narratives with deeper operational detail that shows how great teams practice modern recruiting and the measurable, real-world impact of the product.

  • Interview customers and write stories yourself, building the kind of trust that gets talent leaders to share the specific, messy details that make a story useful.

  • Track how each story performs by channel and use what you learn to shape the next one.

  • Work with internal partners on a plan for refreshing existing case studies and updating outdated ones.

  • Partner with Marketing to bring the strongest stories into key brand moments like Ashby One.

  • Work with our multimedia team on video and creative formats. You'll own the customer relationship and the story, and they'll own production, so the best customers end up in the most memorable formats.

You'll bring editorial taste and a deep read on the TA zeitgeist to make stories that feel unmistakably Ashby.

Collaborate with our Partnerships and CS teams to develop customer advocacy and reference programs.

They run strategic activation for our talent community, and you'll make sure the content and resources that show up in their in-person activations and engagement campaigns are sharp, clear, and genuinely useful to the founders and talent leaders in the room.

  • Establish clear systems for tracking advocacy contributions across content, product feedback, event participation, and references.

  • Build a reference process that protects customer time while giving Sales, Marketing, and Comms access to the strength of our user base.

  • Create meaningful ways to thank customers that stay objective and never cross ethical lines.

  • Work with Partnerships on joint customer stories, partner references, and co-marketing.

  • Partner with CS, Product, and RevOps so that insights and contributions flow back into the business.

Capture and amplify organic love from the community.

Each week, dozens of practitioners share unprompted stories about Ashby, our product, our sales cycle, our reliability, and our people. We capture some of it on our Ashby Wall of Love, but there's far more out there than we collect today.

  • Turn sentiment into assets people use, from testimonial moments to themed compilations to category education pieces.

  • Treat organic love as a sourcing channel, routing the best posts toward case studies, references, and employee content.

Your work will help prospects and the broader TA world see what our customers experience every day.

Help every team with customer story enablement.
You'll build the enablement structure that helps GTM teams tell customer stories with confidence, so one great conversation can become employee posts, sales references, and community moments.

  • Partner with Sales leadership to build customer stories into the Sales motion, matching stories to industries, regions, deal stages, etc.

  • Equip CSMs to share customer stories themselves on LinkedIn

  • Package every story into ready-to-use kits for employees, Sales, and CS.

  • Build feedback loops with Sales and CS to track which stories help win and keep customers, and where there are gaps in our customer stories

  • Measure across the program, including story pipeline, reference turnaround, organic mentions captured, employee participation, and influence on pipeline.

When this works, you'll be able to show how one great customer conversation turned into dozens of moments across the market.

You will probably love this role if…

  • You get more out of a great interview than a great byline. Much of the job is helping customers and employees sound like their best selves, and most of your best work will carry someone else’s name.

  • You like working across teams and getting things done through trust rather than authority, since CS, Sales, People, Partnerships, and Comms all touch this work.

  • You get real energy from customer stories, both the tactical workflow optimizations to the emotional transformation that comes with great hiring.

  • You see case studies not as artifacts, but as a strategic engine that shapes brand, community, and pipeline and you know how to develop case studies that both showcase the customer and hit on Ashby’s differentiation or market hesitation.

  • You have strong editorial taste and a knack for spotting the story inside the story.

  • You value nuance, ethics, and relationship-building. You never push a customer to say something that doesn’t feel natural or fair.

  • You’re as comfortable with operational rigor (tracking, tagging, measurement) as you are with creative storytelling and narrative craft.

  • You want to be part of a team that deeply believes content and community are the heart of modern GTM.

This role is not for you if…

  • You only want 0 to 1 work. You’ll build new programs, but you’ll also run and improve a case study program and a reference process that already work.

  • You see advocates as a resource to extract from. This role depends on protecting customer time and never crossing ethical lines, even when Sales needs a reference by Friday.

  • You’re looking for a traditional case-study writer role focused on turning out assets on request.

  • You’re uncomfortable interviewing customers, synthesizing complex stories, or navigating sensitive feedback.

  • You’re not interested in learning the product deeply or building intuition about TA practitioners’ workflows, pressures, and culture.

  • You need AI to write your first draft. We believe AI has its uses, but at Ashby we believe people should drive the thinking, and the first draft is where most of the thinking happens.

Interview Plan

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. We’ll dive into past projects and simulate working together via project working sessions. Our interview process is:

  • 30-minute intro call (Recruiter Screen)

  • 45-minute interview with Chris Frakes (Hiring Manager)

  • 30-minute interview with Anum Hussain

  • A take home assignment reviewed by the hiring panel

  • A virtual on-site (1 hour) with

    • Rosalia Cefalu, Head of PMM

    • Hannah Small, Partnerships Team and Former Startup Sales AE

  • A 30-minute final round with our VP of Marketing, Harriet Johnston

Benefits

  • Competitive salary and equity.

  • Opportunity to work with a talented and passionate team.

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅.

  • Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

  • Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

  • $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

  • If you’re in the US, top-notch health insurance for you and your dependents with all premiums covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.
